_readme: Machine-readable project status. Read this at the start of a session to orient; update it at the end of any task that changes what's built or what's broken. Prose belongs in the docs — this file is the ledger. Status values: not_started | in_progress | complete | blocked.
current_phase: Two rigs now. ANDY/M2: verified and calibrated 2026-08-12, but marine Ch 16 is NOT receivable at his location with the stock antenna indoors (hardware.md 4) - unchanged. PARKER/UCA202: brought up 2026-09-07 and Ch 16 IS receivable there, which unblocks marine corpus collection for the project. His rig is calibrated (floor -41.1, thresholds -34.1/-38.1) with the radio IN THE WINDOW at volume 13/31 - both settings matter and both are currently held by nothing but a note. Real marine audio, real ASR and real Coast Guard traffic are all in the database. Capture rate against a human listening on an identical radio ranged from 6-of-6 in a good session to 1-of-8 and 2-of-8 in poor ones; the misses are transmissions that never broke the radio squelch, which is fixed in the codeplug by the fire department and cannot be changed. More RF at the radio is therefore the only remaining lever, and a telescopic whip (Nagoya NA-773, SMA-FEMALE for Parker's male port) is on order. PAUSED here pending that antenna. Next session: install it, re-run the ear-log comparison protocol, then hand-label a subset of the 1.3 GB corpus and run evaluate.py - that is what turns the two deliberately-unfixed findings (est_snr_db does not measure intelligibility; the hysteresis window straddles squelch-open hiss) into measured decisions rather than guesses.

phase_0_skeleton.notes: Exit criterion verified 2026-07-30. The Phase 0 refuse-non-16kHz behavior was replaced in Phase 2 by automatic resampling; archival WAV was replaced in Phase 3 by Opus+AAC (WAV remains the no-ffmpeg fallback).

phase_1_transcription_detection.notes: All code items landed 2026-08-10: asr/ (mlx + faster_whisper behind Transcriber, warmup at startup), detect/ (hallucination gates, watchword matcher with phonetic guards per D14, LLM classifier with hard graceful degradation, severity resolution per architecture §5.5), incidents/correlator.py, scripts/replay.py + evaluate.py. 113 tests pass; ruff and mypy --strict clean. REMAINING (corpus-dependent, not code): hand-label data/labels.jsonl, run evaluate.py for a precision/recall baseline, and the base.en/small.en/medium.en WER comparison. Note: neither Whisper engine has been exercised against real audio yet — the first `python -m vhfwatch.pipeline --source file --path <wav>` run downloads the model (~500 MB) and is the real smoke test.

phase_2_live_audio.notes: All CODE items landed 2026-08-10. HARDWARE: docs/hardware.md §5 steps 3, 4 and 5 now PASS on the M2 rig (2026-08-12) — device selection, channel slice, level, and a clean 30 s recording. Thresholds in Andy's config.toml are measured, not guessed. REMAINING for 'complete': §5 step 6, the 30-minute segment-count exit criterion during busy traffic. bringup_log.notes: First entry written 2026-08-12 for the M2 rig. Knob positions still missing.

andy_m2.notes: Verified and calibrated 2026-08-12. Radio on M2 INPUT 2, so use_channel = 1 (input 1 carries Andy's XLR mic). Connected via Thunderbolt dock, which measured 12 dB quieter in the voice band than direct USB-C - keep the dock. SETTLED GAIN STAGING: radio volume 3/4, M2 input 2 trim 90 deg, which inverts hardware.md 3.5's default for a measured reason (docs/decisions.md D18). At that setting: speech peaks -7.6 dBFS, zero clipped samples, idle floor -68.1 dBFS - measured twice either side of a failed re-staging experiment and reproducible to 0.3 dB by hand. 60 Hz pickup on the idle line is self-cancelling and deliberately unfiltered (D17). Knobs still need physically taping. No squelch control on this radio; no macOS input slider exists for the M2.

parker_uca202.notes: Calibrated 2026-09-07, then RECALIBRATED the same evening after the radio was moved into the window and the volume dropped 17->13 to stop clipping: floor -41.1 dBFS, open -34.1, close -38.1 (same D19 offsets, floor+7 and floor+3). NOT yet verified against a real transmission - whether clipping is gone and whether speech still clears -34.1 are both unknown until the next capture. Note calibrate.py was run THREE times: the first run showed a 3.8 dB p90 spread that sits under its 6 dB instability warning and would have put close_threshold within 0.2 dB of p90; two repeats gave p90 == median exactly. Do not paste a single run into config. Radio on RCA left, use_channel = 0. Level set by the radio volume knob alone (the UCA202 has no input trim — the front knob is headphone output only) and TAPED, but the knob POSITION was never written down. Speech peaks -9.2 dBFS, no clipping. Floor -38.3 dBFS with p90 == median (0.0 dB spread over 30 s) — rock steady, and owner-confirmed as the operating baseline (radio in normal monitoring state, nothing transmitting), but 30 dB above the M2 rig's -68.1 with the squelch closed on BOTH rigs, cause not yet diagnosed. Thresholds deliberately deviate from the usual offsets: open = floor + 7 (not +10, because measured variability is zero), hysteresis 4 dB (not 6, because a 6 dB close threshold would land exactly on the floor and the gate would never close). See docs/decisions.md D19 — this is a provisional setting with an open defect behind it, not a settled property of the rig.

known_issues.description: The clips in audio-test-samples/ (and their 16 kHz conversions in data/corpus/) were recorded from the radio's speaker through a laptop mic, NOT through the line-in chain. They are useful only as smoke-test input for the pipeline. Do not tune segmenter thresholds against them, do not treat their noise floors (-60 to -77 dBFS) as representative, and do not use them for the Phase 1 WER comparison — wait for real line-in corpus audio.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07: real ASR has now run end to end on real radio audio (Parker's rig, ch 7 test transmission, mlx-whisper small.en). The pipeline segmented 2 transmissions, transcribed both, archived Opus, and wrote to the DB with 0 pre-ASR rejects, 0 post-ASR rejects and 0 queue drops. faster-whisper is still exercised only at import/signature level.

FIXED 2026-09-07, same day it was found (see the fix commit; regression tests in tests/test_asr.py and tests/test_hallucination.py, 122 tests pass, ruff and mypy --strict clean). Verified by re-running the pipeline over the recording that exposed it: the transcript with the NaN now logs transcript.checks_unrunnable and the one with a real value does not. ORIGINAL REPORT: on the first real ASR run, mlx-whisper returns avg_logprob as NaN (not missing) on many segments — 4 of 5 whisper segments in the ch 7 test. Consequences chain badly. (1) asr/base.py merge_segments duration-weights the values, so a SINGLE NaN segment makes the merged avg_logprob NaN for the whole transmission. (2) At the gate, detect/hallucination.py line 56 tests `t.avg_logprob is not None and t.avg_logprob < threshold`, and NaN < -1.0 is False, so the check silently passes — the `is not None` guard never fires because the value is NaN, not None. (3) Written to SQLite, NaN is stored as NULL, which is why the transcript row reads None and masks the cause. Net effect: the logprob half of the post-ASR hallucination gate is INERT, and in the observed case it failed open on the LOWER-quality of the two segments — the one with a spurious '!' token and a mangled position readback, i.e. exactly what it exists to catch. no_speech_prob still functions, so the gate is degraded rather than absent. AGENTS.md calls detect/hallucination.py load-bearing. Fix direction: treat NaN as MISSING (math.isnan) in merge_segments so it stops poisoning the merged score, and make the gate LOG that the logprob check could not run rather than passing silently. Note failing closed would be wrong here: NaN appeared on 4 of 5 segments, so rejecting on unknown logprob would discard most real transcripts — the project accepts missed detections but not blind ones, and an unrunnable check is an uncertainty to surface (the web app already renders honest uncertainty) rather than a reason to drop evidence. Needs a regression test with a NaN segment; no current test covers it, which is how this reached real audio.

First measured transcription quality on real radio audio (Parker's rig, 2026-09-07, small.en, chain 30 dB compromised): call signs, position minutes and persons-on-board counts were all corrupted. 'test station one' -> 'position one'; 'three six minutes north' dropped entirely; 'one two two degrees' -> 'one, two, two screens'; 'two one minutes west' -> 'one minute west'; 'Three persons on board' -> 'persons on board'. Degrees numbers survived ('four seven' -> '47'). This is a BASELINE on a known-bad audio chain, not a verdict on model choice — it should be re-measured after the 43 dB noise problem is diagnosed, and it is the first real input to the base.en/small.en/medium.en WER comparison. It also concretely validates the architecture's insistence that original audio stay reachable from every alert: a human hears the position correctly, the ASR does not.
LiveAudioSource's disconnect/reconnect path is untested against a real USB unplug — it needs a deliberate yank test during bring-up.

Still unverified on that rig: §5 step 5 (no recording has been written to disk — the meter ran without --record), step 6 (segmentation against real traffic), and the radio's programming (channel, modulation, bandwidth, tone squelch are owner-confirmed on Andy's radio but NOT on Parker's). Andy's M2 knobs are at the settled setting (radio volume 3/4, M2 input 2 trim 90 deg; docs/decisions.md D18) and re-verified, but are NOT physically taped. A bump silently invalidates open_threshold_db, and the pipeline's noise-floor drift warning is the only thing that would catch it.

The M2 measured 12 dB quieter in the voice band through the Thunderbolt dock than connected directly to the laptop on battery, with identical mains content. Reproducible but unexplained; suspected USB power-rail switching noise reaching the bus-powered interface. Keep the dock. Matters because it means the audio chain has a 12 dB failure mode triggered by nothing more than re-plugging a cable.

TX inhibit is unverified on Andy's monitoring NX-5200 and is deliberately untested, since testing it means transmitting. Do not press PTT on the monitoring radio. Modulation, bandwidth and tone squelch are owner-confirmed correct as of 2026-08-12.

Gain staging on the M2 rig inverts docs/hardware.md 3.5's default ordering, and this is measured, not preference: the 60 Hz interference is picked up on the cable downstream of the radio's volume knob, so the interface trim cannot improve SNR. Moving gain from radio to interface raised the idle floor from -68.4 to -38.0 dBFS and caused clipping. Radio high / trim low is correct here (docs/decisions.md D18). Anyone 'fixing' this back to 1/3 radio volume will silently break detection.

Parker's UCA202 rig measures a -38.3 dBFS noise floor against the M2 rig's -68.1 — a 30 dB gap between two rigs running the same radio model with the squelch closed on both, so it is a chain defect and not open-squelch hiss (an earlier reading of this data wrongly assumed the latter). The floor is extremely stable (p90 == median), and a 13 dB crest factor points at broadband amp or converter noise rather than a ground loop. Consequence: the gate sits near -31 instead of -58, so weak and distant stations are lost. Accepted provisionally by the rig's owner so the rig can be used now (AGENTS.md: missed detections are acceptable), but it is expected to be diagnosed, not filed away. The gain-staging hypothesis is FALSIFIED: Parker's volume knob is 17 of 0-31, BELOW Andy's 3/4 (~23), yet peak-to-floor is 29.1 dB against Andy's 60.5 dB — 31 dB less usable range with the radio turned DOWN further, so the radio's own amp is not the source and the noise enters downstream of the volume control (cable, UCA202, USB power, or charger). This makes the rig a second instance of D18, not its opposite: input_gain_db sits downstream of the noise and cannot improve SNR, and turning the radio UP would help but is capped near 3 dB by ADC headroom. That measurement was run 2026-09-07 and CLEARS the interface: UCA202 alone with nothing on its inputs reads -88.8 dBFS (p90 -88.7), its own converter floor and 20 dB below the entire M2 chain. Interface, USB power and host are eliminated; all ~50 dB enters from the radio side of the RCA cable. This does not exonerate the radio — noise injected into its output stage AFTER its volume control (a charger being the obvious candidate) would not scale with the knob and fits the data. Remaining split is charger vs radio output vs cable pickup; the charger A/B (battery-only, then charging) separates them in two 30-second runs. The rig is not inherently limited: a floor matching or beating Andy's is available in principle once the source is found. The charger A/B test (battery vs charging, idle vs during a transmission) is the cheapest next discriminator and has still not been run. See docs/decisions.md D19.

FIXED 2026-09-07 (see docs/decisions.md D20). phonetic_min_similarity raised 0.70 -> 0.85, and multi-word terms now require EVERY token to clear phonetic_min_token_similarity (0.80) against its counterpart rather than scoring the joined string. All ten observed false positives are silent, including three verbatim real transcripts, while every distress phrase still fires. The cost is recorded and deliberate: mated -> mayday (0.760) is now missed, which was D14 canonical example, because it scores BELOW my/made/monday at 0.800 and no threshold separates them. 139 tests pass; ruff and mypy --strict clean. ORIGINAL REPORT: found on the first real Ch 16 transmission ever processed: the phonetic watchword pass produces false positives on extremely common radio words. Measured against config/watchwords.example.toml: 'my' -> mayday (score 0.80), 'made' -> mayday (0.80), 'maybe' -> mayday (0.79), and 'going to' -> 'going down' (0.92). All are CRITICAL terms. Two distinct causes. (1) detect/watchwords.py applies phonetic_min_token_len (4) to the TERM's tokens, not to the MATCHED text, so a 2-character word like 'my' is allowed to match a 6-character term like 'mayday'; a length-ratio guard between term and matched token is missing. (2) Multi-word terms combine per-token scores into an average, so one exactly-matching token ('going') carries a garbage second token ('to' vs 'down') over the similarity floor; every token should have to clear its own bar. The suppress list catches specific cases ('monday') but a blocklist cannot scale to 'my'. Severity resolution limited the blast radius correctly - phonetic hits resolve to WATCH, not CRITICAL, per architecture 5.5 - but an incident was still opened with confidence 0.915. On a busy channel this would fire on a large fraction of all traffic, which is the exact failure D12 warns about: users trained to silence the app. AGENTS.md is explicit that missed detections are acceptable and false positives are not. Note this is precisely the evidence D14 named as its revisit condition, arriving from real audio rather than from evaluate.py.

DESIGN GAP found 2026-09-07 on 2h14m of real traffic: est_snr_db does not measure intelligibility, and on an FM receiver it cannot. Once squelch opens, the recovered audio LEVEL is constant regardless of signal strength - only its QUALITY degrades - so a metric based on level above the muted-line floor is decoupled from whether anything is readable. Concretely: a 17-second Coast Guard broadcast scored est_snr_db 16.3 dB and was UNINTELLIGIBLE to Whisper, which returned the single character '!' across raw, normalised and high-passed variants. The audio genuinely is speech-shaped - broadband, with the top 12 spectral bins holding 0.97% of the energy and an envelope modulation peak at 3.11 Hz, squarely syllabic - it is simply too degraded to read. Consequence: hallucination.min_snr_db (3.0) is a pre-ASR gate that every marginal transmission on this rig will pass, handing unreadable audio to a model this project documents as hallucinating confidently on noise. This time it emitted '!' rather than a sentence, which is luck rather than a guarantee. Nothing is behaving contrary to spec, so this is a gap and not a bug. A candidate replacement metric is in-band quality rather than level - voice-band-to-hiss ratio, or the 3-8 Hz syllabic modulation ratio, which measured 1.52 on this segment against a >2 expectation for clean speech. NOT changed yet: one observation is not enough to retune a load-bearing gate, and the corpus now exists to measure it properly.

TUNING finding 2026-09-07: on Parker's rig the segmenter hysteresis window straddles squelch-open hiss, so one spoken transmission became a 59-second segment. Measured levels around the 13:59 broadcast: -40.7 dBFS before, -19 during, then -36.4 for fifteen seconds AFTER the voice stopped - the radio stays unmuted with hiss. close_threshold_db is -38.1, BELOW that hiss, so once the gate opens it cannot close until the squelch itself closes. open_threshold_db (-34.1) is correctly ABOVE the hiss, so hiss alone will not start a segment. The root of it: calibrate.py measures the squelch-CLOSED line (-41.1), but this rig has a third level calibration never sees - squelch-open hiss at about -36.4 - and any close threshold below it holds segments open. Raising close to about -35.5 would close promptly but leaves only ~1.4 dB of hysteresis, which carries its own risk. NOT changed yet; one observation is not enough, and the effect is inflated segment duration plus trailing hiss fed to ASR rather than lost detections.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07 by moving the radio from the desk into the WINDOW - nothing else changed. Capture went from 1-of-8 to 6-of-6 against a human listening on an identical radio. The diagnosis chain below is kept because the reasoning matters and several hypotheses were wrong: both radios are the same model with squelch fixed in the codeplug by the fire department communications chief (Parker may not change it) and they were SIDE BY SIDE during the morning traffic, which eliminated siting, model, squelch programming, tone squelch and channel. The leading hypothesis had become computer RFI desensing the radio through the audio cable; that is now unlikely, because the audio noise floor barely moved between positions (-38.1 desk to -37.7 window) while reception transformed. It was position: at VHF a few feet and a window frame is enough. TWO RESIDUAL PROBLEMS remain. (1) Two of the six transmissions arrived as 0.2 s blips and were discarded by min_duration_ms=600, one of them the only distress-adjacent traffic of the day (towing a boat taking on water); loosening min_duration would not help, since the squelch opened and shut and there are only 0.2 s of audio - marginal signals are still lost and the loss is silent. (2) Every strong capture now CLIPS at peak_dbfs 0.2, which is newly cheap to fix: speech lands at -8.7 to -10.5 dBFS RMS against a -38 floor, 28 dB of SNR, so the radio volume can drop ~10 dB (17 to about 13-14) and still leave 18 dB of margin. The window position is currently held by nothing but memory and should be physically marked. ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS: MEASURED 2026-09-07, and it reframes what limits this rig: the radio's SQUELCH is the real detection threshold, not open_threshold_db. Over 30.3 minutes the voice band shows exactly one event (10:44:23, lifting 44.9 dB above the floor); the next largest thing in the whole recording lifts 3.8 dB for 0.1 s, which is noise. Nothing exists in between. That bimodality is squelch behaving as a hard RF gate - a signal either breaks it and arrives fully quieting, or the audio output stays muted and NOTHING reaches the capture chain. It is why the event count is identical at floor+4 and floor+10 dB: every threshold across a 40 dB range performs the same because there is no signal population in that range to discriminate. Two consequences. (1) D19's +7-vs-+10 threshold reasoning is largely moot on this rig - keep the setting, but it does not buy the sensitivity that argument implied. (2) The operator heard 3 transmissions by ear on a second radio (10:31, 10:38, 10:44) and the rig captured 1; the two misses contain no signal at all in the recording (voice-band excursion 0.6 and 2.8 dB across +/-90 s), so they were lost at the RF stage and NO software change recovers them. Confound to resolve: the second radio is a different receiver, possibly better sited or with different squelch, so part of the gap may be that rather than the antenna - the clean test is both radios side by side. This makes the antenna the measured top priority rather than the theoretical one. ORIGINAL NOTE: Ch 16 IS receivable at Parker's site, unlike Andy's - confirmed 2026-09-07 by a 30-minute recording that captured one real marine transmission at 10:44:23 PDT, strong enough to clip. This is the first marine corpus audio the project has, and it unblocks marine corpus collection at this location. CORRECTED 2026-09-07, same day: the earlier reading of 'traffic volume is very low' was WRONG and must not be used for the Phase 4 watchdog threshold. A second 20-minute session (11:45-12:05 PDT) recorded ZERO events - largest voice-band excursion 4.4 dB against 44.9 dB for a real transmission - while the operator listening on a second handheld in the same house logged FIVE transmissions in four minutes (11:47-11:50), including a readable exchange with a vessel identifying as Corvesta. The site has ample Ch 16 traffic; the monitoring receiver cannot hear it. Note which transmission the rig DID catch this morning: the one that arrived hot enough to CLIP at 0 dBFS. The rig appears to receive only signals strong enough to overload the input, which is a large sensitivity deficit rather than a weak-signal edge case - the 11:48-11:50 transmissions were readable by ear and still produced nothing. The audio chain is eliminated as a cause: the recording floor is -38.1 dBFS, matching every session with the radio connected, versus -88.8 with the UCA202's inputs open, so cable, interface, host, capture code and thresholds are all fine and the fault is entirely upstream of the audio. Candidates, now reordered after further analysis. (1) PROGRAMMED SQUELCH LEVEL - the leading hypothesis. 'No accessible squelch control' has been read throughout these docs as 'squelch is not adjustable', which is wrong for a commercial radio: on the NX-5000 series squelch level is a per-channel parameter in the CODEPLUG, not a knob. A tight programmed squelch on Ch 16 would produce exactly the observed behaviour - silence for everything except an overwhelming local station. Free immediate test: most Kenwood commercial portables have a Monitor / squelch-off side key that forces squelch open. Press it during traffic. Rushing noise THEN transmissions means squelch level is the fault and it is a programming change (hardware.md 3.6 already treats squelch-open as a deliberate option); rushing noise and nothing else means RF is not reaching the radio and the antenna/position is next. (2) antenna not seated, damaged or missing; (3) position and shielding - the monitoring radio sits beside a laptop, dock and USB supplies while the operator's other radio moves around; (4) a CTCSS/DCS receive tone on Ch 16, confirmed absent on Andy's radio but NEVER confirmed on Parker's; (5) wrong channel or zone. Candidate 4 is weakened but not excluded by the 10:44 capture. Supporting evidence that this is longstanding behaviour rather than a regression: across both sessions the operator heard 8 transmissions by ear and the rig captured 1, and the one it caught arrived hot enough to CLIP. The two sessions are also spectrally IDENTICAL - same mains-dominant idle signature, same band rolloff, same DC, same peak character - so nothing in the chain changed between them. A third scan ran Whisper over the entire 20-minute empty session in 30 s chunks normalised to near full scale and found ZERO speech segments, which is telling because Whisper is documented in this project as hallucinating readily on noise; it produced nothing at all. Finally, the physics rules out 'faint speech under the noise': FM squelch is binary and the AF level is set by the volume control, not by signal strength, so a weak station gives full-level scratchy audio rather than quiet audio. Absence of audio therefore means the squelch never opened, not that the signal was too quiet to record. The decisive test is free: both radios side by side in the same spot during traffic, then swap antennas between them. This is hardware.md section 5 step 1, still unticked on BOTH rigs after two sessions, and it is exactly the situation that step exists to prevent.

FIXED 2026-09-07 by dropping the radio volume 17 -> 13 of 0-31 and recalibrating (floor -41.1, thresholds -34.1/-38.1). Verified against 2h14m of real traffic: 49 clipped samples in an 18 s event (0.006%) versus 2844 and 6698 (~1%) at volume 17, a ~150x reduction, with speech peaking at -9.9 dBFS RMS and 24 dB of margin over the gate. Capture rate did NOT suffer: the transmissions missed in that session show voice-band lifts of 1.4-4.5 dB against a 4.4 dB noise ceiling measured on a definitively empty session, so the audio never arrived and the squelch never opened. ORIGINAL REPORT: Parker's rig CLIPS on real strong traffic: the 2026-09-07 Ch 16 transmission hit 0.00 dBFS with 6698 clipped samples (1.16% of the window). The level was set against a ch 7 test transmission peaking at -9.2 dBFS, which was not the loudest signal the system would see - hardware.md 3.5 warns about exactly this and Andy avoided it by calibrating against a nearby radio at full quieting. The bind is that this rig cannot simply turn the radio down: the noise enters DOWNSTREAM of the volume knob (D19), so lowering the knob drops signal while the floor stays put, costing SNR at the quiet end where this rig already has none to spare. Clipping happens at the UCA202's ADC and the radio's volume is the only control upstream of it, so there is no other stage to use. This makes the undiagnosed ~43 dB noise problem a concrete capability cost rather than an untidy number: with Andy's 60 dB of range both headroom and sensitivity fit, with Parker's ~30 dB they do not.

Marine Ch 16 is not receivable at the POC site (Andy's house, stock rubber duck indoors), confirming the hardware.md 4 warning. The system cannot currently do its actual job at this location no matter how well the pipeline works. Highest-value fix is an antenna (telescopic whip or mag-mount + SMA adapter, in a window with a view of the water), or recording the marine corpus somewhere better sited.

Segmenter verification will run against strong rebroadcast fire traffic, not marine traffic. This validates segmentation LOGIC (thresholds, hang time, pre-roll, fragmentation) but NOT weak-signal sensitivity: a central-station rebroadcast arrives fully quieting while a distant vessel does not. Do not promote 'segmentation works' to 'we would hear a mayday'. Also note 'mayday' is standard fireground vocabulary for a firefighter in trouble, so watchword hits on this corpus are not false positives in the marine sense, and the marine-loaded ASR initial_prompt may hurt WER here.

docs/hardware.md §5 step 4 — signal present on the configured channel, phase cancellation ruled out (45 dB idle-to-signal jump), speech peaks -8.4 dBFS with zero clipped samples after trimming down ~10.5 dB.
docs/hardware.md §5 step 5 — 30 s recording verified: no flat line, no clipping. Noise floor -68.4 dBFS, p90 within 0.1 dB.

open_questions: What is the actual traffic volume on Ch 16 at a site that can RECEIVE it? Unanswerable at the current location. Still sets the Phase 4 'no transmission in N hours' watchdog threshold (placeholder 6 hours) and determines whether closed-squelch VAD leaves too much on the table.
Will an external antenna make Ch 16 receivable at Andy's house, or does the POC need to run somewhere else entirely?
